top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on a clean, general mechanism, the magic-wavelength condition that cancels the trap light shift, which is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. It has been reproduced in many independent laboratories and has opened new regimes such as millimetre-scale gravitational redshift and many-body effects in clocks. The two-name allocation to Katori and Ye is the cleanest credit on the shortlist; the citation should rest on the lattice and magic wavelength, not on the 10^-18 record that will be superseded. No award is a clearly worse outcome than this mature achievement.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no connection to Katori or Ye, only the general Gothenburg physics proximity to Chalmers colleagues
